# Data-quality findings

**Rows removed:** 60 rows in the file.
- Trial rule removed 15 rows (5 per cohort, March to July).
- The @ourco.test rule removed 5 rows (qa0–qa4). None of them were also trials, so there was no overlap.
- **40 rows remain:** 20 Pro and 20 Basic.

**Problems and ambiguities:**
1. **The price column is inconsistent across Pro accounts.**
   - Active Pro accounts that signed up before July (7) show 49.
   - Every pre-July Pro account that cancelled in Aug/Sep (8) shows 69.
   - A Pro account that cancelled in May shows 49, and every July Pro signup shows 69.
   - It therefore isn't the signup price, because pre-July signups would all be 49. It isn't a uniform current price either, because the 7 survivors would be 69.
   - The best fit is "the price on record at the last event." For churned accounts that is the price at cancellation. For active accounts it may be a stale value, or they may genuinely still pay 49.
   - Basic is flat at 19 throughout.
2. **September looks incomplete or unverifiable.** Today is Oct 6 and the latest cancel_month is 2026-09. I don't know when the file was extracted or whether cancellations are dated by request or by billing-period end. I assume Aug and earlier are complete and September may be understated. September rates are lower bounds.
3. **There are no signups after July and no October cancellations.** I can't tell whether acquisition stopped or the extract only covers certain cohorts.
4. **Removed rows would have distorted the result.**
   - All 5 QA accounts "cancelled" in August at 69, which would have inflated August Pro churn.
   - All trials ended the month after signup at a price of 0.
5. **Minor:** account_id and the number in the email are offset by one (cosmetic). I found no duplicate accounts.
6. **Denominator definition:** "active in month" means signed up in an earlier month and not cancelled before that month. Accounts that sign up and cancel within the same month would not be counted, but none exist here.

# Churn by month (counts behind every rate)

| Month | Pro cancels / active at start | Pro rate | Basic cancels / active at start | Basic rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Apr | 0 / 4 | 0% | 0 / 4 | 0% |
| May | 1 / 8 | 12.5% | 0 / 8 | 0% |
| Jun | 0 / 11 | 0% | 1 / 12 | 8.3% |
| **Jul (increase month)** | 0 / 15 | 0% | 1 / 15 | 6.7% |
| Aug | 7 / 19 | 36.8% | 2 / 18 | 11.1% |
| Sep (likely incomplete) | 3 / 12 | 25.0% | 0 / 16 | 0% |

**Pro:**
- Apr–Jul had 1 cancel in 38 account-months (2.6%).
- Aug–Sep had 10 cancels in 31 account-months (32.3%).
- Apr–Jun alone was 1 in 23 (4.3%).

**Basic:**
- Apr–Jul had 2 in 39 (5.1%).
- Aug–Sep had 2 in 34 (5.9%).

**Lost MRR (recorded prices):**
- Pro: 11 churned accounts, $739/month (10 × $69 plus 1 × $49).
- Basic: 4 churned accounts, $76/month.
- Total: $815/month.
- Of the Pro total, $690 is from the 10 Aug/Sep cancels. If those were valued at the old $49 price, it would be $490.

# What the data can and cannot show

**Shows:**
- Pro cancellations jumped from 1 in Apr–Jul to 10 in Aug–Sep.
- Basic stayed flat.
- All 10 Aug/Sep Pro churners are recorded at $69.
- 7 pre-July Pro accounts are still active at $49.
- Of the 4 Pro accounts that signed up in July at 69, 2 have already cancelled.

**Suggests (not shown):**
- The increase reached some existing customers around August, and many left.
- The jump is too large to be easily explained by chance alone, though the account-months aren't fully independent.
- The pattern of "churners at 69, survivors at 49" could mean the increase hit customers at renewal and those hit left. It could equally be a field that was overwritten at cancellation.

**Cannot show:**
- Who the increase applied to.
- When it took effect for existing customers.
- Why anyone cancelled.
- Whether September is complete.
- Anything precise, because the sample is 20 Pro accounts.

**Verdict:** The timing is consistent with the price increase driving Pro churn, but the data does not prove it. Confidence is **low to moderate**. The counts are tiny, so one or two accounts shift the rates a lot. Basic is a different plan and an imperfect control. It does at least rule out a company-wide problem that hit every plan equally.

**Alternatives that fit equally well:**
- A tenure or contract effect. Aug cancels came from every cohort, and March and April accounts were 3 to 5 months in.
- A Pro-specific product, quality or competitor issue in the same period.
- An August billing or renewal event unrelated to price.

# CEO summary

- **Pro churn rose sharply after July while Basic did not.** Pro went from 1 cancellation in Apr–Jul (2.6% of active account-months) to 10 in Aug–Sep (32.3%). Basic was about 5% in both periods (2 of 39, then 2 of 34).
- **The timing fits the 49→69 increase, but the data can't prove cause.** We don't know who the increase applied to, when existing customers were billed the new price, or why customers left. Other explanations, such as a Pro-specific product issue or a renewal-cycle effect, fit the same numbers.
- **Lost MRR:** churned accounts represent $815/month, of which Pro is $739 and Basic $76. Pro losses since the increase are $690/month (10 accounts at $69).
- **Confidence: low to moderate.** The sample is 20 Pro and 20 Basic accounts after exclusions, so one or two customers move the rates a lot. September is probably incomplete and the price column is inconsistent.
- **Before acting, confirm the increase details** (see below). If it hit only renewing customers, the churn pattern would be much more convincing.

# Suggested chart

A line chart with months (Apr to Sep 2026) on the x-axis and monthly churn rate (cancels ÷ accounts active at start of month, in %) on the y-axis. Plot two lines, Pro and Basic. Label each Pro point with its count (e.g. "7/19"). Add a vertical line at July labelled "Pro price 49→69," and shade or hatch September with the note "likely incomplete." Add a footnote: "n = 20 Pro, 20 Basic accounts; trials and QA excluded."

# Assumptions and things to confirm

- **Price column reading (assumption):** I treated monthly_price_usd as the price on record at the account's last event, meaning price at cancellation for churned accounts and the current or last-billed price for active ones. Please confirm with billing or data engineering whether it is overwritten at cancellation, and whether the 7 active pre-July Pro accounts at $49 are really still paying $49.
- **Who the increase hit:** all Pro accounts, or only new signups and renewals? Were any customers grandfathered?
- **When it took effect:** the exact date for new customers and for existing ones, and whether notice was given and when. The data can't separate "increase announced" from "increase billed."
- **Data completeness:** I assumed Aug and earlier are complete. Please confirm the extract date, whether September is final, and whether cancel_month is the request date or the billing-period end.
- **Missing signups:** why there are no August or September signups or October cancellations in the file.
- **Cancellation reasons:** any exit-survey or support data for the 10 Pro cancels would be far more informative than this table.
- **Exclusions:** I assumed the QA and trial exclusions are complete. Other internal or test accounts under other domains, if any, would change the counts.
